extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: TextVQA contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing data. In the first stage, annotators identified images that did not contain text. In the second stage, 1-2 questions were collected for each image. In the third stage, 10 answers were collected for each question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images that did not contain text and noisy data from annotators were filtered out. Questions were removed if a majority of workers marked them as having no text in the image, not being a question, not requiring reading to answer, or being unanswerable. Hand-crafted questions were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were shown an image and asked to provide a question which requires reading the text in the image to answer. To collect a second question, annotators were shown the first question and asked to come up with a different question requiring reasoning about the text. 10 answers were collected for each question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to endow Visual Question Answering (VQA) models with the ability to read text in images, which is a dominant category of questions asked by visually impaired users of their assistive devices.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model often answers questions about cities with 'new york', indicating a bias in city-related questions. The most common answer ('yes') is the majority answer for 4.71% of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The model has a strong dependency on the quality of OCR tokens produced; if the OCR module misses text, the output can be wrong. The OCR model fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., a scribble), or partially occluded.
